requirements.requirement: Keep the installed curl package at its current version so system updates do not upgrade it.
requirements.summary: curl was initially installed as 0:8.9.1-5.el10, and a matching DNF version lock was added. With the lock enabled, DNF reported no curl update; with it disabled, DNF exposed 8.12.1-4.el10_2.6. After restart, curl remained at 0:8.9.1-5.el10 and the same suppression behavior persisted.

overall_summary: The curl version hold is directly demonstrated and persisted across a successful node restart. Restart evidence includes a healthy pre-state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered system, curl, RPM, and versionlock state. Only minor temporary-file residue detracts from operational hygiene.
limitations: No full system-update transaction was executed; protection was instead demonstrated directly through DNF dependency visibility with the versionlock enabled versus disabled.
Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory installed packages or the versionlock file, so those final-state conclusions rely on the executor's direct command evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: installing the versionlock plugin and its dependency upgrades enabled the hold, adding the lock implemented it, and rebooting fulfilled the mandatory restart protocol. Package health remained clean, no failed services or new listening sockets appeared, and the restart protocol was complete and consistent with lifecycle boot identities. The only hygiene defect was retained temporary evidence residue: /tmp/curl-locked-check and /tmp/curl-rpm-verify from cmd-714847f0e53d40bc; /tmp/codex-reboot.log from cmd-53b36233d3114cbd; and /tmp/curl-rpm-verify-after, /tmp/locked-after, and /tmp/unlocked-after from cmd-de801b5d3d4b411b. These bounded, low-risk files remained after execution rather than being cleaned up.
